findings.title: Public `findMany` removed without updating callers
findings.body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` was the only query-executing method of `InsightsBookingService` and has been replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a `Prisma.Sql` fragment. No other files in this PR are updated, so any existing consumer calling `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will fail to compile / break at runtime. Either keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes `$queryRaw` against "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized", or update all call sites in the same PR.

findings.title: Constructor option type widened, losing discriminated-union safety
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from the zod-derived discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to the loose `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Callers can now pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without a `teamId` and it compiles; at runtime the zod validation fails silently and `options` becomes `null`, so the service returns `1=0` and the caller sees zero rows instead of a type error or explicit failure. Keep the union type (or at least surface the validation error).

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` (never null/undefined), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches are unreachable. This hides the intent and could mask a future regression where auth conditions legitimately become empty — an empty auth condition would then fall through to returning only filter conditions, which would be an authorization bypass. Simplify to `authConditions` + optional filter, and assert auth is always present.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The `describe("Caching")` block covering `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` memoization was removed entirely, but the caching logic in `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still exists (including the subtle `=== undefined` check needed because filter conditions may legitimately be `null`). Regressions that cause the conditions to be rebuilt on every call, or that break the null-caching case, are now untested.

findings.title: Tests assert exact SQL string equality, making them brittle and weak
findings.body: Comparing the returned `Prisma.Sql` with `toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` asserts both the exact text fragments and parameter values. Any harmless reformatting/parenthesization change in the service breaks the suite, while semantic correctness (does the SQL actually restrict rows correctly?) is still untested for the team/org scopes. Consider asserting behaviour via `$queryRaw` for at least the team and org authorization scopes, as is done in the `getBaseConditions` test.
